angle: Strategic property upgrade for long-term wealth
body_text:
If your household income is $20K/month,
but your property is under $1.5M…
you could be losing $40K+ a year without realising it.

Hey, it’s Alvin Ang here.

I used to be a mortgage banker, years spent analysing loans, risk profiles

And why some families upgrade once… while others upgrade twice or three times.

Here’s what I realised:

Most people don’t make bad property choices.

They make bad property strategies.

And every year you wait, your options quietly shrink:

✅ Your loan tenure shortens (you’re a year older)

✅ Prices move up while your cash stays the same

✅ Peers who moved earlier are already on their next upgrade

So the real question isn’t

“Should I upgrade?”

It’s: “What do I want my property to DO for me over the next 10 years?”

Here are some insights you may not know:

INSIGHT #1: Buying the biggest condo you can afford often limits your future.

I’ve seen families stretch for a large 4-bedroom

Only to realise 3 years later they had zero flexibility to invest or upgrade again.

INSIGHT #2: Playing it ‘safe’ can be just as risky.

Some chose cheaper condos hoping to be conservative…

And ended up watching their neighbours upgrade twice while they stayed stuck.

INSIGHT #3: One big home vs split strategy is not a lifestyle question

It’s a strategy decision.

Each path affects cash flow, flexibility, and your next move very differently.

That’s why I created The Strategic Upgrader’s Framework 

For HDB owners who want clarity before making a million-dollar decision.

Inside the free guide, you’ll learn:

✅ The FRAME Method, 5 factors that determine the right upgrade strategy for YOU

✅ Why “buying the biggest condo you can afford” can kill flexibility (and what to do instead)

✅ 3 projects worth considering this year with strong upside potential

This is for you if:

✔ Household income is $20K and above

✔ You’ve just reached MOP (or are close)

✔ You want a 10-year property plan, not just “a nicer home”

Click Learn More and I’ll send it over.

No pressure, no hard sell.
